findings.title: Shared permission-decorator request state permits cross-request privilege confusion
findings.attacker: Authenticated lower Admin with concurrent access while a Super Admin invokes the same decorated handler and HTTP method in the same worker
findings.invariant: Each request must be authorized using its own principal.
findings.dataflow: A lower Admin sends a serializer-valid PUT /api/admin/user containing their own id and admin_type='Super Admin'. AdminRoleRequiredMiddleware admits ordinary Admins. BasePermissionDecorator stores the request in a class-held decorator instance. If another thread invokes that same decorator with a Super Admin request after the attacker's assignment but before its permission check reads self.request, the check uses the Super Admin principal. The wrapper then invokes self.func with the attacker's original args, allowing the attacker-controlled role/password/MFA mutation.
findings.impact: Conditional Admin-to-Super-Admin escalation and account takeover; sibling super_admin_required operations have the same primitive.

evidence.snippet:
@validate_serializer(EditUserSerializer)
@super_admin_required
def put(self, request):
...
user = User.objects.get(id=data["id"])
...
user.admin_type = data["admin_type"]
...
user.set_password(data["password"])
...
user.save()

counterevidence: account/middleware.py:36-41 independently rejects anonymous and Regular User requests under /api/admin/, so this evidence does not establish anonymous-to-admin escalation.
Only the same decorated function shares a request slot; concurrent GET does not authorize PUT.
The vulnerable scheduling window is narrow. SessionRecordMiddleware:25 evaluates authentication before the handler, so the check normally does not trigger a lazy-user database fetch.
No concurrent runtime experiment was executed; exploitation frequency is unknown.
Serializer validation constrains fields but explicitly permits Super Admin as admin_type.
findings.remediation: Keep the decorator stateless: pass the original request as a local argument into check_permission(request), and use that same local request for disabled checks. Add a controlled concurrent regression test proving a lower Admin request cannot borrow another request's principal.

findings.title: Disabled administrators retain access through middleware-only admin handlers
findings.attacker: An administrator whose account has been disabled while their existing browser session remains valid
findings.invariant: Disabling an account must revoke access to authenticated administrative operations.
findings.dataflow: Super Admin account editing assigns user.is_disabled and saves without revoking sessions or necessarily changing the password. On a subsequent existing-session request, AdminRoleRequiredMiddleware checks authentication and admin role but not is_disabled. Several contest admin handlers have no BasePermissionDecorator disabled check; ensure_created_by likewise checks only role and ownership. The disabled Admin can continue using those handlers for owned contests.
findings.impact: Account disabling fails to revoke contest creation/editing and owned-contest submission export.

evidence.snippet:
user.admin_type = data["admin_type"]
user.is_disabled = data["is_disabled"]
...
if data["password"]:
    user.set_password(data["password"])
...
user.save()

contest = Contest.objects.get(id=contest_id)
ensure_created_by(contest, request.user)
...
zip_path = self._dump_submissions(contest, exclude_admin)

counterevidence: New password login rejects disabled users in account/views/oj.py:157-158.
API-key authentication rejects disabled users in account/middleware.py:15.
Handlers protected by BasePermissionDecorator reject disabled users at account/decorators.py:26-27.
Ownership checks still restrict ordinary Admins to their own objects.
Requires an existing session and retained administrator role; does not confer a new role.
findings.remediation: Enforce is_disabled centrally for authenticated session requests, including middleware-only admin handlers; revoke existing sessions when disabling accounts. Add a regression covering an already-authenticated Admin disabled without a password change.

findings.title: Contest helper authorizes a participant-selected contest but mutates globally selected ranks
findings.attacker: Authenticated lower Admin who can access at least one visible contest
findings.invariant: Contest administration must require ownership or Super Admin status, and rank mutations must belong to the authorized contest.
findings.dataflow: PUT /api/admin/contest/acm_helper supplies contest_id, rank_id, problem_id and checked. The global middleware requires only Admin role. check_contest_permission('ranks') permits any authenticated participant of an accessible contest; it does not require contest administration. The handler then fetches rank_id without contest filtering and changes submission_info[problem_id]['checked']. An attacker can authorize their own public contest and target a rank in a separate private or invisible contest.
findings.impact: Unauthorized modification of another organizer's contest helper records. The sibling GET additionally exposes real names and helper data for accessible contests to non-owner Admins.

evidence.snippet:
class ACMContesHelperSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    contest_id = serializers.IntegerField()
    problem_id = serializers.CharField()
    rank_id = serializers.IntegerField()
    checked = serializers.BooleanField()

counterevidence: Global admin middleware blocks ordinary users and anonymous callers.
The chosen authorization contest must pass visibility/password/start/rank restrictions, but an attacker can use an accessible contest they own.
Target rank and problem entries must exist; integer rank IDs are not secrets.
The mutation changes the checked helper flag, not score or accepted status.
findings.remediation: Require request.user.is_contest_admin(self.contest) for both helper methods and fetch the rank with pk=data['rank_id'], contest=self.contest. Add cross-owner and mismatched-contest negative tests.

findings.title: Public user leaderboard bypasses real-name privacy filtering
findings.invariant: Users' real names are withheld from other users and non-owner public serializers.
findings.dataflow: Anonymous GET /api/user_rank enters undecorated UserRankAPI.get, queries enabled Regular User profiles with submissions or score, and serializes all UserProfile model fields using RankInfoSerializer. Unlike UserProfileSerializer and UsernameSerializer, RankInfoSerializer does not replace the model real_name field with a permission-aware method. Pagination permits enumeration of leaderboard users and their real names.
findings.impact: Public disclosure of real-name-to-username mappings and other complete profile fields for leaderboard participants.

evidence.snippet:
real_name = serializers.SerializerMethodField()
...
self.show_real_name = kwargs.pop("show_real_name", False)
...
return obj.real_name if self.show_real_name else None

self.need_real_name = kwargs.pop("need_real_name", False)
...
return obj.userprofile.real_name if self.need_real_name else None

counterevidence: Only enabled Regular Users meeting leaderboard activity filters are exposed.
No password, MFA seed, API key or session token is included.
The separate profile endpoint deliberately hides other users' real names, supplying source evidence that the leaderboard disclosure violates intended privacy.
findings.remediation: Give RankInfoSerializer an explicit public-field allowlist that excludes real_name and private profile details, or reuse the existing permission-aware real-name serialization.

resolved_questions.question: Policy inheritance
resolved_questions.resolution: No SECURITY.md in any assigned directory. Parent independently confirmed absence across repository and ancestors. The permitted resolver launcher was attempted for all three directories but silently exited without a payload.

resolved_questions.question: Authentication and recovery direct bypass
resolved_questions.resolution: No additional direct anonymous login/MFA/reset-token bypass established. Login authenticates the password before MFA; change-password/email authenticate the current user and check enabled MFA. Recovery validates CAPTCHA, a random token and expiration, then clears token and intentionally disables MFA. rand_str uses Django get_random_string for all but its first character, so the single random.choice character does not make tokens predictable.

resolved_questions.question: API keys and SSO
resolved_questions.resolution: API-key authentication requires enabled OpenAPI and non-disabled owner, and possession intentionally skips CSRF. Keys are generated from the secure random helper. Public SSO POST is a bearer-token identity lookup; no tokenless authentication or role mutation established. Long-lived SSO tokens are a hardening concern, not a demonstrated bypass.

resolved_questions.question: Session deletion
resolved_questions.resolution: SessionManagementAPI.delete deletes a supplied session key before ownership checking, but exploiting another session requires possession of its unpredictable bearer key. No independent route to obtain another user's key was established; not reported as an exploitable finding.

resolved_questions.question: Account mass assignment
resolved_questions.resolution: EditUserProfileSerializer has an explicit writable-field set; unrelated role/counter fields are discarded by serializer validation. Super Admin editing explicitly allows privilege changes but is protected subject to the shared-decorator race.

resolved_questions.question: Announcement and contest rich text
resolved_questions.resolution: RichTextField invokes XSSHtml on database preparation. Full sanitizer inspection found scheme normalization for links, attribute allowlists and escaping; no modern-browser source-to-execution XSS chain established within the available backend source. Immediate create/update responses can retain the caller's unsanitized in-memory value, but no cross-user or CSRF-deliverable exploit was established.

resolved_questions.question: Submission archive filenames
resolved_questions.resolution: Export constructs ZIP entry names using usernames and problem display IDs. These can contain traversal-looking components, but this path uses writestr rather than filesystem extraction and no unsafe downstream extractor was established. Do not report this as server-side arbitrary file write.

resolved_questions.question: Credential leads
resolved_questions.resolution: oj/settings.py contains a hardcoded Sentry DSN with credential-shaped URL components. It was not used, checked remotely, or reproduced here. Context supports an error-ingestion configuration rather than OJ authentication, host administration or RCE credentials. Deployment database credentials are environment-derived.

resolved_questions.question: Tests and execution boundary
resolved_questions.resolution: All assigned tests were read, not executed. PermissionDecoratorTest contains placeholder tests; existing tests do not cover concurrent decorators, disabled existing admin sessions, helper cross-contest authorization or public real-name filtering. No application code, network requests, edits, history or alternate revisions were used.
